changes_made.explanation: Normalized task names to standard forms, removed 'Other:' prefix. Consolidated repetitive output descriptions. Removed duplicate LLama2-13B-Chat model entry. Added Mistral-7B which was mentioned in TravelPlanner experiments. Added Code Generation as a distinct task based on Codenames Collaborative results.
Consolidated duplicate metric entries and normalized capitalization consistently. All metrics are explicitly mentioned in the paper under different evaluation sections.

Minor capitalization normalization. The paper clearly uses LLMs as judges in the selection phase to evaluate agent quality based on inheritance of characteristics and maintenance of differences from parent agents.

No human evaluation is explicitly mentioned in the paper. The paper states: 'we do not manually evaluate the quality of the generated agents, but the results show that EVOAGENT significantly improves the performance of LLM-based agent on complex tasks.'

overall_notes: The paper focuses on automatically generating multi-agent systems using evolutionary algorithms, with NLG tasks as the primary evaluation domain. The extraction was generally accurate but needed normalization of task names and consolidation of duplicate entries. The paper extensively evaluates generated outputs but relies solely on automatic metrics and LLM-as-judge approaches without human evaluation.
